steps.title: Prewarm 16‑well station
steps.instruction: Place the ECIS 16‑well station in a 37 °C incubator at least one day before the experiment to pre‑warm the array holder and fill the incubator water reservoir to prevent the wells from drying out.

steps.title: Prepare coating reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions needed for array coating:

substeps.instruction: L‑cysteine 100 mM stock: dissolve 12.12 mg L‑cysteine in 1 mL sterile Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter, store at 4 °C (stable ≤2 weeks).
Dilute the stock 10× with sterile Milli‑Q water to obtain 10 mM L‑cysteine; for two arrays prepare 3 500 µL of 10 mM solution by mixing 350 µL 100 mM stock with 3 150 µL sterile Milli‑Q water.
0.1 % acetic acid solution: add 25 µL glacial acetic acid to 25 mL sterile Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.

Collagen/0.1 % acetic acid coating solution: for 17 wells (16 experimental + 1 extra) add 27.2 µL rat‑tail collagen type I (5 mg/mL) to 5 072.8 µL of the 0.1 % acetic acid solution (gives 10 µg collagen per cm²; each well growth area = 0.8 cm²).

steps.title: Coat array wells
steps.instruction: Apply the coating solutions to the ECIS arrays:

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of the 10 mM L‑cysteine solution to each well, incubate 30–45 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash wells twice with 300 µL sterile Milli‑Q water.
Add 300 µL of the collagen/0.1 % acetic acid solution to each well, incubate 60 min at RT.
Wash wells twice with 300 µL sterile Milli‑Q water.
Add 400 µL of Ad‑DF+++ medium to each well and keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Calibrate ECIS and record baseline
steps.instruction: Set up the ECIS instrument and acquire a baseline before seeding cells:

substeps.instruction: Turn on the computer and the ECIS Zθ instrument.
Open the ECIS software.
Place the test array in the 16‑well station, click **Setup**, and verify connections (green = good, red = bad); repeat until all wells show green.
Select the RC test array from the array‑type drop‑down and run the RC check; confirm that 8W1E wells read ~5 nF and 8W10E wells read ~50 nF.
Choose the desired acquisition mode (e.g., Multiple Frequency/Time).
Click **Start**, enter a file name, and record baseline measurements for at least 30 min while harvesting cells.

steps.title: Harvest and dissociate organoids
steps.instruction: Obtain a single‑cell suspension from 3‑D intestinal organoids:

substeps.instruction: Remove organoid culture medium and add cold Ad‑DF+++ (0.5 mL per well in a 24‑well plate or 1 mL per well in a 12‑well plate).
Pipette up and down several times with a P1000 to disrupt the Matrigel and transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard the supernatant.
Add 1–3 mL TrypLE Express (volume depends on pellet size), resuspend the pellet and incubate 5–7 min at 37 °C in a water bath.
Vigorously resuspend cells 15–20 times with a P1000 (place a 200 µL tip on top of the 1000 µL tip) to obtain a single‑cell suspension with no visible clumps.
Inactivate TrypLE by adding 10 mL Ad‑DF+++, then spin at 340 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in Human IntestiCult organoid growth medium (OGM) supplemented with ROCK‑inhibitor (1 µL ROCK‑i per mL, i.e., 1:1000).
Count cells and adjust the suspension to contain 150 000–300 000 cells per well (volume adjusted with OGM+ROCK‑i).

steps.title: Seed cells onto coated array
steps.instruction: Plate the organoid‑derived single cells on the prepared ECIS wells:

substeps.instruction: Pause baseline acquisition in the ECIS software.
Remove the array from the incubator and aspirate the Ad‑DF+++ from each well.
Add 400 µL of the cell suspension (150 k–300 k cells) to each well; include at least one well that receives only medium as an empty control.
Return the array to the 16‑well station and click **Resume** to continue data acquisition.

steps.title: Set measurement frequencies
steps.instruction: Configure the ECIS software for data analysis:

substeps.instruction: Use the default 4 000 Hz frequency for real‑time resistance monitoring.
For post‑experiment analysis, extract capacitance data at 64 kHz (optimal for detecting electrode coverage) and resistance data at 500 Hz (optimal for barrier integrity).
Click **Pause** to halt acquisition (the experimental clock continues).
Remove the array under a laminar‑flow hood and replace the medium with ROCK‑inhibitor‑free medium 2–3 days after seeding.
Refresh the medium every 2–4 days thereafter.
Return the array to the holder, click **Check**, wait 5–10 min for temperature equilibration, then click **Resume**.

steps.title: Induce differentiation (optional)
steps.instruction: Switch to differentiation medium to obtain mature intestinal cell types:

substeps.instruction: After the monolayer reaches the capacitance plateau (≈118 h), replace OGM with Human IntestiCult organoid differentiation medium (ODM).
Continue ECIS monitoring; resistance typically increases further as cells differentiate.

steps.title: Perform wound‑healing assay (optional)
steps.instruction: Create a controlled electrical wound in a confluent monolayer:

substeps.instruction: Select the wells to be wounded in the ECIS software.

Open **Wound/Electroporate Setup**, choose **Wound**, and set the parameters: current = 5 000 µA, frequency = 50 000 Hz, duration = 60 s (the 4 000 µA, 30 s setting is insufficient for complete wounding).
Optionally set a delay using **Delay until hour**.
Click **Activate** to apply the wound.
Resume acquisition to monitor wound closure over time.

description:
Validation of protocol The protocol described in this paper has undergone a meticulous optimization process
through a series of experiments to ensure its effectiveness. For this protocol
paper, several smaller experiments were conducted to illustrate crucial findings
that guarantee a successful experiment. These smaller experiments aimed to highlight
key insights and refine procedural details. Multiple replicates were carried out for
each experimental condition, with careful consideration given to the distribution of
replicates across two arrays. This approach not only validates the protocol's
robustness but also ensures its adaptability and reliability across various
conditions. This protocol has been validated and used in the following research article: ten Hove
et al. [9].
